title: EnergyCal attenuation of routed-expert Muon updates in a tiny MoE
setting: A small top-2 sparse MoE (one residual MoE layer with 4-16 ReLU experts) is trained on sklearn digits for 250 minibatch steps with Muon (5-step quintic Newton-Schulz, Nesterov momentum 0.95, decoupled weight decay), with Adam for the router. The treatment rescales each routed-expert matrix update by a factor derived from the normalized squared Frobenius norm of its Newton-Schulz direction. The metric is the thresholded loss-spike burden of the training-loss trace (mean excess over the trailing 20-step median at steps exceeding 1.5x that median); held-out test loss and accuracy are reported as endpoint checks.

paper.title: EnergyCal: Taming Loss Spikes in Muon-Family Optimizers for Sparse MoE Training
paper.claim: Attenuating routed-expert updates by a post-Newton-Schulz energy coefficient reduces loss-spike burden of plain Muon at matched nominal learning rate and weight decay without hurting the endpoint.

metric.name: spike_burden
metric.description: Sum over steps (after a 20-step warm start) of the training loss minus its trailing 20-step median, counted only where loss exceeds 1.5x that median, divided by the number of evaluated steps. Diagnostics: final_test_loss and test_acc on held-out samples, spike_frac (fraction of flagged steps), mean_q (mean routed-expert scale factor).

factors.name: method
factors.description: muon: plain Muon. energycal: routed-expert update scaled by q=clip((||D||_F^2/(d*0.8))^p,0,1) with p=1 per expert matrix (assumed form from the paper's Eq. 5). uniform_scale: routed-expert update scaled by a constant 0.6, a non-energy-dependent control for simple magnitude reduction.

factors.name: lr
factors.description: Nominal Muon matrix learning rate, from stable to spike-prone.

factors.name: n_experts
factors.description: Number of routed experts (top-2 routing); more experts means sparser traffic per expert and more low-token updates.
